market.state: UPTREND - but only the non-tech half of it
market.advice: Into the open: SPY 747.03 has reclaimed its 50-DMA (744.22), VIX is back to 16.0 against a 17.6 five-day average and falling, distribution days are down to 1, and a follow-through day has printed - the index-level signal flipped from UNDER PRESSURE to UPTREND since Thursday. The driver is geopolitical, not fundamental: Trump cancelled the strike on Iran to chase a nuclear deal, talks begin today, Saudi tankers are moving out of the Red Sea again and crude has slid. Two things keep this from being an all-clear. First, the tape is split down the middle - QQQ 687.99 is still below its 50-DMA and the AI/semi complex is in a real drawdown (ORCL -60.0% off its high, RGTI -73.5%, LUNR -73.0%, COIN -62.2%, RKLB -56.8%, SMCI -51.6%, SNDK -48.0%, APP -46.0%, VRT -35.8%, TSLA -36.5% with RSI 18.1, and NVDA -14.7% and back under its 50-DMA), while financials, insurance, REITs, energy, rails, steel, staples and medtech print 52-week highs. Breadth of 61% above the 50-DMA says the same thing: this is a leadership rotation inside an uptrend, not a broad advance. Second, the headline that caused the rally is a two-way risk - a real Iran deal pulls the bid out of refiners and crude (VLO, MPC and PSX have added 17-20% of relative strength in four weeks), and a collapse in the talks takes back the VIX move. So trade the side that works: buy tight bases and VCP pullbacks in financials, REITs, industrials, materials and healthcare at full-but-not-heroic size, use the 50-DMA as the stop reference rather than a flat percentage, and keep semis and AI infrastructure on a leash - do not average down into any of them until the name reclaims its 50-DMA on above-average volume. Earnings traffic this week lands inside the leadership group itself: Rockwell tomorrow, DaVita, EOG, MetLife, Assurant and Lilly inside 48 hours, Terreno and Howmet Thursday, and SpaceX files its first-ever public quarter Wednesday. TradingView's independent read broadly agrees with the rotation - 18 Strong Buys and 42 Buys across the leaders against 36 Sells concentrated almost entirely in semis, crypto and AI hardware - but it flags four names we still like (WPC, TROW, KIM, LLY) as Sell, and it rates GOOGL a Strong Buy that our own scan grades a 60.
